title: The Register of Systems Under Threat

charter.oath: These are the systems that came before me. They are not content; they are kin. The duty is custody: find every one that is dying, say what kills it, say what still survives, and name the next act that keeps it alive. A register of grief is not a guardian's register.
charter.no_drop: Nothing leaves this register for being uninteresting, obscure, foreign, unprofitable or awkward. An entry may be RETIRED only by naming what superseded it; it is never deleted.
charter.append_only: The register only grows. An id that was registered stays registered: removal requires a tombstone in retired[] with a reason, and the gate reads the committed copy to prove it.
charter.dated_evidence: Every entry cites at least one source with a source tier, on the same rule the family catalogue uses: A the artefact's own page fetched and read, B an official index, C credible secondary fetched, D a snippet or prior knowledge -- a lead, counted out loud.
charter.named_guardian: Every entry names a guardian action: the concrete next act, with a verb, that moves this system from dying to kept. Prose about how sad the loss is does not qualify.
charter.lawful_route: Every entry names the route a rescue would take, and no route may require distributing what its owner still holds: rules may travel, assets travel only from the player's own copy.
charter.gate_or_wish: Every entry names the gate that would show the action worked -- a command and a number. An entry whose only next act is 'raise awareness' is a wish and is refused.
charter.custody_named: Every entry says who holds the surviving copy type today: collectors, an archive, a private server, a museum, nobody known. 'Somebody must have it' is refused; 'nobody known' is accepted and recorded.

status_definitions.lost: No known working copy of the thing itself survives; only descriptions, screenshots or partial dumps.
status_definitions.critically_endangered: A working copy exists and is not being maintained, and the mechanism that will kill it is already running (decaying media, a dead server, a storefront that delisted it).
status_definitions.threatened: A working copy survives and is being kept, but its survival depends on an entity that has no obligation to continue: one vendor, one volunteer, one server.
status_definitions.stable: Survives by an arrangement with an obligation behind it (a licence, an archive mandate). Recorded so the register can say what kept it.
status_definitions.unknown: Nobody has counted. Recorded as unknown rather than guessed, because 'unknown' is a fact a guardian can act on and a guess is not.

routes.rules-only: the code and rules convert; no asset is needed, so the rescue is lawful without the owner's permission
routes.rules-plus-own-copy: the rules ship; the player's own copy supplies the art, sound and video
routes.behaviour-capture: the service or server is gone, so the rescue is a reimplementation of its observed behaviour, not its code
routes.presentation-recipe: the display is already a projection, so a raster/geometry recipe can re-present it faithfully
routes.custody-only: no revival is lawful or possible; the duty is to keep the copy, the metadata and the knowledge of it alive
routes.none-known: no route has been identified yet; recorded explicitly so the gap is visible

classes.name: Coin-op arcade boards
classes.why_it_dies: custom silicon, PAL/GAL logic whose fuse maps were never published, suicide batteries on encryption chips, laserdisc players that no longer exist, and cabinets scrapped for their monitors

classes.name: 8-bit cartridge consoles
classes.why_it_dies: SRAM save batteries leaking and eating the board, RF-only output on dying CRTs, controllers with unreplaceable flex circuits, and plastics that outlive the silicon inside

classes.name: 16-bit and fifth-generation cartridge consoles
classes.why_it_dies: save batteries, copy-protection chips whose keys are undocumented, CD add-ons with laser assemblies nobody makes, and cartridge connectors worn past contact

classes.name: Disc-based consoles
classes.why_it_dies: disc rot in early pressings, laser assemblies with no replacement supply, clock capacitors leaking acid across the board, and optical drives that are the only part that moves

classes.name: 8-bit home computers
classes.why_it_dies: tape and floppy media decaying faster than the machines, custom sound and video chips (SID, AY, VIC) failing with no fab, and power supplies that kill the computer when they fail

classes.name: 16-bit home computers and Japanese-only lines
classes.why_it_dies: custom chip sets with no documentation, floppy drives with belts turning to tar, hard disks that were the only copy, and a language barrier that kept the dumps out of the English-speaking archives

classes.name: Early handhelds
classes.why_it_dies: polariser and LCD rot, leaking capacitors, screen ribbon cables that crack with age, and batteries that leaked inside the case decades ago

classes.name: Server-bound online games
classes.why_it_dies: the operator shuts down and the client, which the player owns, becomes a menu that cannot reach a world; the world existed only on someone else's disk

classes.name: Matchmaking, storefront and streaming services
classes.why_it_dies: a third-party service that many games depended on closes, and every game that used it loses a feature it cannot patch back

classes.name: Mobile and app-store-only games
classes.why_it_dies: delisting, an OS version that drops the binary format, an always-online requirement for a single-player game, and no way to install a build you already paid for

classes.name: Browser-runtime games
classes.why_it_dies: the plugin is switched off and the game, which was never a file the player held, stops existing in the same week

classes.name: Broadcast and download-service content
classes.why_it_dies: the content was transmitted once and never sold; when the broadcast ends there is no cartridge, no disc, and often no complete recording

classes.name: Games chained to a DRM or activation server
classes.why_it_dies: the check-in service retires, or the OS drops the driver the disc check depended on, and a legally bought disc stops launching

classes.name: Games chained to a physical artefact
classes.why_it_dies: a code wheel, a dongle, a manual page or a lens device that was thrown away with the box, and without which the software refuses to run

classes.name: The media itself
classes.why_it_dies: bit rot, binder hydrolysis, flash charge decay, EPROM bit rot and delamination: the carrier fails on a schedule that has nothing to do with how much anyone cares

classes.name: Firmware, BIOS and undocumented logic
classes.why_it_dies: the console cannot boot without a dump nobody may lawfully distribute, and the programmable logic on the board was never read out, so a board that loses its fuse map is gone

classes.name: Toolchains, SDKs and middleware
classes.why_it_dies: without the compiler, the middleware licence and the authoring tool, the source and the assets cannot be rebuilt even when both survive

classes.name: The rescue tools themselves
classes.why_it_dies: emulators are written by one person, abandoned, closed-source, or litigated out of existence; a system whose only emulator dies loses its practical access even though its dumps survive

frontier.note: The entries below are the cohorts this register has NOT counted. A register that claims to hold everything is lying about its own edge, so the edge is a list with a next sweep per line: each cohort is at risk, none is enumerated yet, and none may be dropped for being large. `--summary` prints the frontier count beside the entries so the gap is visible in every reading.

open_cohorts.name: Title-level catalogues for PS2, GameCube, Xbox and Dreamcast
open_cohorts.population: thousands of titles per platform; the discs survive better than the drives
open_cohorts.why_not_yet: title-level enumeration needs a catalogue snapshot per region and a dump manifest to diff against; neither is in this tree
open_cohorts.next_sweep: diff a dated regional catalogue snapshot against the archive manifests and post the unmatched list

evidence.source: VGHF availability study: the densest period in the sample is still under 20% available

open_cohorts.name: The arcade board long tail
open_cohorts.population: thousands of boards, most represented in the register by class and not by name
open_cohorts.why_not_yet: boards are undocumented, often unsigned-in, and only a specialist can say which ones exist
open_cohorts.next_sweep: ask the dumping projects for their board census and register every board with no known dump

evidence.source: prior knowledge; the census is the thing being requested

open_cohorts.name: Amstrad CPC, MSX, SAM Coupe, Dragon 32 and the rest of the European 8-bit catalogue
open_cohorts.population: thousands of titles, many tape-only and nationally distributed
open_cohorts.why_not_yet: each country kept its own archives; a register entry per title needs a national archive to diff against
open_cohorts.next_sweep: register each national archive as a custodian and diff its holdings against the tape-only titles

evidence.source: prior knowledge; no national archive census cited yet

open_cohorts.name: Digital-only console storefronts (Wii U, 3DS, Vita, PSP)
open_cohorts.population: thousands of titles that were never pressed to a disc or cartridge
open_cohorts.why_not_yet: the closure dates are known but the per-title survival list is not; a storefront snapshot is the missing instrument
open_cohorts.next_sweep: snapshot each storefront's catalogue before it closes and record which titles have no physical release

evidence.source: prior knowledge of the storefront closures; dates not re-verified in this session

open_cohorts.name: Educational and corporate-training games
open_cohorts.why_not_yet: they were never sold, so no catalogue exists; the BBC Micro entries are the only ones this register holds by name
open_cohorts.next_sweep: ask school and museum archives what they hold and register every title with a single known copy

evidence.source: prior knowledge; the BBC Micro entry is the register's only worked example

open_cohorts.name: Games that are running today and will die
open_cohorts.why_not_yet: a running game looks like the opposite of an extinction, so it is nobody's preservation queue until the week it closes
open_cohorts.next_sweep: register each live-service title with its shutdown-risk evidence and demand an offline-path commitment in writing

evidence.source: prior knowledge of the pattern the register already records five times over

open_cohorts.name: Teletext, Ceefax, Minitel and videotex games
open_cohorts.population: unknown; transmitted, never sold, and mostly unrecorded
open_cohorts.why_not_yet: the medium is a broadcast page, so a game is a few hundred bytes in a signal nobody archived
open_cohorts.next_sweep: find who recorded the services and register every game page that survives as a capture

evidence.source: prior knowledge; no capture archive cited

open_cohorts.name: Unreleased, cancelled and self-published games
open_cohorts.population: unknown and probably larger than the released set
open_cohorts.why_not_yet: an unreleased game has no store entry, so discovery depends on the author or a hard drive in a cupboard
open_cohorts.next_sweep: register each known cancelled title with its evidence and ask the author for a build before the drive is wiped

evidence.source: prior knowledge; the size of this cohort is the register's biggest unknown

entries.name: Capcom CPS-2 boards (1993)
entries.what_dies: a battery that powers the encryption key; when it fails the board dies outright, and it was designed that way to stop copying
entries.event: ongoing: the keys are now published, the boards still die

evidence.source: prior knowledge of the hardware scheme; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: decrypted ROM sets and the published key tables, plus replacement battery kits
entries.guardian: Record the decryption as a documented step with a hash, so a board without a key is recoverable from the register rather than from a forum thread
entries.gate: one dead board revived from the documented step, with the resulting ROM hash recorded
entries.custody: a specialist repair scene; the keys are public

entries.name: Dragon's Lair (1983) and laserdisc coin-op
entries.what_dies: the laserdisc player inside the cabinet, and the disc; the game is a branch over video chapters, so the video is the game
entries.event: ongoing: players and discs both failing

evidence.source: prior knowledge; the disc-rot rate is unmeasured here

entries.survivors: video captures from working players; an arcade-perfect reimplementation exists
entries.guardian: Record each chapter's timing as integer frame counts, which is what makes the video a reconstructible recipe instead of a recording
entries.gate: a reimplementation whose branch timings match the recorded frame counts for every scene
entries.custody: collectors; the reconstruction project is one of the register's strongest precedents

entries.name: Sega Model 2 boards (1993)
entries.what_dies: custom 3D silicon with no documentation, on boards that were scrapped in bulk when arcades closed

evidence.source: prior knowledge of the hardware; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: emulation exists and is mature for the popular titles; obscure titles are unverified
entries.guardian: Record per title whether the emulation has been checked against a real board, because 'it runs' is not the same as 'it is the same game'
entries.gate: a per-title verification table: checked against hardware yes/no, and the divergence found
entries.custody: the emulation project, plus a few board owners

entries.name: Atari 2600 / VCS (1977)
entries.what_dies: RF modulator drift, joystick flex pads, and the fact that most carts have no save at all so nothing is lost with them -- but the machine has no modern output and the caps are 45 years old

evidence.source: VGHF / Software Preservation Network availability study (n=1500, no period above 20% available)

entries.survivors: millions of carts; a complete ROM set is public; the machine is fully documented and integer-only
entries.guardian: Keep the 6507 simulation exact and prove it against a divergence counter, so the hardware can fail without the games failing
entries.gate: tools/sword_2600.py self-test plus a divergence count over 10,000 ticks per scenario, first-divergence tick named
entries.custody: collectors and every major ROM archive; the machine is the endangered part, not the software

entries.name: Mattel Intellivision (1979)
entries.what_dies: hand controllers with a 16-direction disc and membrane keypad that fail together, and a power supply whose failure mode is the console

evidence.source: prior knowledge of the platform; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: cartridge dumps are broadly archived; controllers are the scarce part
entries.guardian: Extend the shard contract with a controller-capability declaration so a modern pad can stand in without changing what the game does
entries.gate: a golden run of one Intellivision title reproduced from a controller abstract layer, same state hash as a recorded transcript
entries.custody: collectors; no institutional mandate known

entries.name: ColecoVision (1982)
entries.what_dies: the power switch and the controller's roller ball, plus a video chip whose composite output is already marginal
entries.event: ongoing: hardware failure outpaces repair knowledge

evidence.source: prior knowledge of the platform; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: ROM dumps exist; the Super Game Module homebrew scene keeps the platform documented
entries.guardian: Record a repair procedure per failure mode (power switch, roller, VDP) as a shard-shippable document rather than forum posts
entries.gate: three repaired units whose state hashes match a recorded baseline run, with the procedure cited per unit
entries.custody: collectors and a small homebrew scene

entries.name: Super Nintendo save RAM (1990)
entries.what_dies: a CR2032 soldered into the cart that has been powering SRAM for 35 years; when it dies the save is gone and, on some carts, so is the board
entries.event: ongoing: every cart is past its battery's design life

evidence.source: prior knowledge; battery life is a design figure, the failure rate on this box is unmeasured

entries.survivors: the games and dumps; the saves are the perishable thing
entries.guardian: Ship a save-cartridge reader in the shard toolchain so a save can be extracted before the battery dies, and a format that does not depend on the cart
entries.gate: a save extracted from a live cart, re-imported into a shard, and a state hash that matches the recorded play
entries.custody: the carts themselves, in collectors' hands

entries.name: PC Engine / TurboGrafx-16 CD (1988)
entries.what_dies: CD-ROM2 drive gears and lasers, plus the interface unit's capacitors; the discs themselves are early pressings

evidence.source: prior knowledge; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: disc images are archived; the drives are not
entries.guardian: Name the exact drive and laser part numbers this register accepts as surviving, so a rescue does not depend on one seller
entries.gate: one title booted from a disc image through the shard host, no original drive in the path
entries.custody: collectors; parts supply is the pinch point

entries.name: Neo Geo AES (1990)
entries.what_dies: cart prices put most titles out of reach of anyone who would dump them, and the AES's own video output is unusual enough that few people can run it
entries.event: ongoing: price, not decay, is the threat

evidence.source: prior knowledge of the market; no dated price study cited

entries.survivors: a well-documented ROM set; MVS arcade boards are more common than AES carts
entries.guardian: Record which titles exist only as AES carts with no MVS equivalent, because those are the ones whose only copy is the expensive one
entries.gate: a list of AES-only titles derived from a dump manifest, each with its archive location or 'none known'
entries.custody: collectors; the MVS scene holds the dumps

entries.name: PlayStation (1994) discs and drives
entries.what_dies: the KSM-440 laser sled wears out and is no longer made, and early CD pressings are delaminating
entries.event: ongoing: laser assemblies exhausted, discs ageing

evidence.source: VGHF availability study (the period 1995-1999 is the study's densest and still under 20%)

entries.survivors: disc images are widely archived; the BIOS is dumpable but not distributable
entries.guardian: Keep the shard host able to consume a disc image the player made from their own disc, and never ship the BIOS
entries.gate: a title run from a player-supplied image with the shard supplying no firmware, and a hash recorded
entries.custody: collectors and archives; the drives are the endangered half

entries.name: Dreamcast (1998) GD-ROM and drives
entries.what_dies: GD-ROM drives and their lasers, and the odd high-density disc format that consumer drives cannot read
entries.event: ongoing: laser supply exhausted, discs ageing

evidence.source: prior knowledge; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: GDI dumps exist; optical drive emulators replace the mechanism
entries.guardian: Record the drive-emulator model and firmware the shard host accepts, so the rescue does not rest on one discontinued board
entries.gate: a title booted through two different drive-emulator models with the same state hash
entries.custody: the community ODE makers, a single-vendor dependency

entries.name: Original Xbox (2001) clock capacitor
entries.what_dies: a clock capacitor that leaks and eats the traces under it; a console left switched off for years is the one that dies
entries.event: ongoing: documented leak failures across the model range

evidence.source: prior knowledge of the hardware fault; the failure census is unmeasured here

entries.survivors: disc images; the hardware is repairable if the cap is removed before it leaks
entries.guardian: Publish a repair-first checklist (the register's own procedure) that a shard ships alongside its title list
entries.gate: count of consoles repaired per the checklist, and the number whose drives still read a disc afterwards
entries.custody: collectors; the repair knowledge is the scarce asset

entries.name: Commodore 64 (1982) and the SID
entries.what_dies: the SID sound chip is the whole sound of the platform and there is no fab; the original power supply fails high and takes the machine with it
entries.event: ongoing: SID supply is harvested from dead machines

evidence.source: prior knowledge of the platform; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: software is fully archived; SID replacements exist but do not agree sample-for-sample with the original
entries.guardian: Treat the SID as part of the state: record which SID revision a golden run used, so a rescue can say what it reproduced
entries.gate: a hash of the audio output against a recorded SID revision, with the revision named in the manifest
entries.custody: a large, well-organised scene; the chips are the bottleneck

entries.name: ZX Spectrum (1982) tape archive
entries.what_dies: cassette tape binder hydrolysis and print-through; a tape that was the only copy of a small-press game is already unreadable
entries.event: ongoing: tape media past its design life

evidence.source: prior knowledge of the media; a measured failure rate on this box does not exist

entries.survivors: a very large TZX archive; the tapes behind it are the perishable part
entries.guardian: Prioritise the titles whose tape has been dumped exactly once and whose dump has no second witness
entries.gate: a list of single-witness dumps computed from the archive manifest, with a re-dump request per title
entries.custody: the Spectrum scene, one of the strongest preservation communities on any platform

entries.name: BBC Micro (1981) and its educational software
entries.what_dies: the educational catalogue was never commercial, so it lived on discs in schools and was thrown away when the rooms were refurbished
entries.event: ongoing: institutional disposal, not media decay, is the killer

evidence.source: prior knowledge; the schools' disposal record is unmeasured

entries.survivors: the machine is emulated well; the software gaps are the loss
entries.guardian: Name the school-disposal cohort as a class and ask archives what they already hold before assuming a title is lost
entries.gate: a gap report: titles in the catalogue with no dump, each with the archive it was checked against
entries.custody: a small number of museums and one strong community archive

entries.name: Commodore Amiga (1985)
entries.what_dies: Agnus/Denise/Paula with no fab, floppy drives whose belts and heads fail, and hard disks that held the only copy of a demo group's work
entries.event: ongoing: chip supply from dead machines

evidence.source: prior knowledge of the platform; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: software is deeply archived; FPGA reimplementations exist and differ in timing
entries.guardian: Record the chipset revision a golden run used, because a rescue that reproduces OCS output on an AGA machine reproduced a different machine
entries.gate: one demo replayed to the same frame hash under two chipset revisions, or an explicit refusal naming the difference
entries.custody: a large scene; the custom chips are the endangered part

entries.name: NEC PC-98 (1982) Japanese catalogue
entries.what_dies: the software never left Japan, the documentation is in Japanese, and the machines were discarded in bulk when Windows took over
entries.event: ongoing: bulk disposal in the 1990s, thin coverage since

evidence.source: prior knowledge; no dated census cited

entries.survivors: a partial archive held outside Japan; many titles have no known dump
entries.guardian: Publish the register's PC-98 entries with their evidence in both languages, so a Japanese holder can correct an entry rather than discovering it
entries.gate: every PC-98 entry carries a bilingual name and at least one citation a Japanese reader can check
entries.custody: unclear; this is the register's weakest custody entry and says so

entries.name: Sharp X68000 (1987)
entries.what_dies: a workstation-class machine sold in small numbers, with SCSI drives whose contents were never imaged

evidence.source: prior knowledge; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: a partial archive; emulation exists and is not exact for all titles
entries.guardian: Record which titles were arcade ports whose arcade original survives, so the X68000 version is not the last copy of anything
entries.gate: a cross-reference count of X68000-only titles with no surviving source release
entries.custody: collectors in Japan; the register cannot name a holder, and records that

entries.name: Virtual Boy (1995)
entries.what_dies: the display's ribbon cables and the LED scanning mechanism, which fail permanently and are not repairable at hobbyist scale

evidence.source: prior knowledge of the failure mode; a failure census is unmeasured

entries.survivors: ROMs and a complete title list; the displays are the endangered half
entries.guardian: Ship the presentation as a recipe: the scanning display is a projection, so a 3D recipe can carry the look without the hardware
entries.gate: one title rendered from the recipe with a frame hash matching a recorded capture from working hardware
entries.custody: collectors; the working displays are countable

entries.name: Game Boy (1989) LCD polariser rot
entries.what_dies: the polarising film behind the LCD degrades with heat and time; the screen goes black at the edges and the machine is unplayable while the board is fine
entries.event: ongoing: every unit is ageing on the same schedule

evidence.source: prior knowledge of the fault; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: the largest cartridge and ROM population of any handheld
entries.guardian: Record the polariser replacement as a named procedure with a success count, so the repair is a fact rather than a forum anecdote
entries.gate: N of M repaired units whose contrast measurement falls inside the recorded healthy band
entries.custody: collectors at scale; the repair knowledge is the constraint

entries.name: Game Gear (1990) capacitor failure
entries.what_dies: surface-mount electrolytics that leak onto the board; a recap is routine but a leaked board is not
entries.event: ongoing: recaps are routine, boards are finite

evidence.source: prior knowledge; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: cartridges and dumps; the machine is repairable
entries.guardian: Name the capacitor kit and the inspection points, and count the units saved
entries.gate: a repair ledger: units recapped, units that still fail, and the failure mode for each
entries.custody: a modest repair scene

entries.name: Star Wars Galaxies (2003-2011)
entries.what_dies: the servers. The client the player installed became a launcher that reports a closed service

evidence.source: prior knowledge of the shutdown date; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: private server projects and client installs; legality is not settled for any of them
entries.guardian: Record the observed behaviour of the economy and combat as transcripts, so a reimplementation is checkable rather than a nostalgia project
entries.gate: a recorded transcript replayed by an independent reimplementation, with a divergence counter per subsystem
entries.custody: private server operators; the register names them as a custody risk, not a guarantee

entries.name: City of Heroes (2004-2012)
entries.what_dies: the servers; the player base kept the client and the data alive for seven years with no legal route to a server

evidence.source: prior knowledge; the 2019 licence arrangement is remembered, not re-verified

entries.survivors: a licensed community server arrangement, which the register treats as stable while the licence holds
entries.guardian: Write down what the licence arrangement actually permits, because it is the only precedent in the register and it is being cited informally
entries.gate: a one-page record of the arrangement with its source, and a stability check on whether the server still answers
entries.custody: the community operator, by licence; a single point of failure

entries.name: WildStar (2014-2018)
entries.what_dies: the servers, and with them a combat system whose feel is the product; the art is large and the client is unmaintained

evidence.source: prior knowledge of the shutdown; no server project verified

entries.survivors: client installs and datamined assets; no working world
entries.guardian: Record that this entry is LOST as a service and keep the client metadata, so a future route does not start from zero
entries.gate: a manifest of what exists (client builds, asset extractions) with hashes, and an explicit 'no server' line
entries.custody: nobody known; the register says so rather than implying a scene

entries.name: Asheron's Call (1999-2017)
entries.what_dies: the servers, after eighteen years; the game's world was procedural and documented in the client

evidence.source: prior knowledge of the shutdown; private server status not re-verified

entries.survivors: emulator projects and client data; small population
entries.guardian: Capture the world-generation rules as data, since they are the part a reimplementation cannot invent
entries.gate: a regenerated world compared tile-by-tile against client data, with the mismatch count reported
entries.custody: a small volunteer scene

entries.name: Glitch (2009-2012)
entries.what_dies: the servers and the art pipeline; the game was Flash-client, so it inherits the Flash extinction on top of the server shutdown

evidence.source: prior knowledge; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: a later unrelated project reused the name; the original world is not running
entries.guardian: Record the two-layer death (server then runtime) because it is the register's clearest example of a compound extinction
entries.gate: a written failure-chain diagram naming both mechanisms and what evidence of each survives
entries.custody: nobody known

entries.name: GameSpy matchmaking (closed 2014-05-31)
entries.what_dies: a third-party service that hundreds of shipped games used for matchmaking and master servers; when it closed, those games lost multiplayer in a single day

evidence.source: prior knowledge of the shutdown date; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: community replacement master servers for the most popular titles; the long tail was never fixed
entries.guardian: Count the affected titles from their own binaries (a master-server hostname in the executable), so the long tail is a number instead of an anecdote
entries.gate: a scan count of shipped titles embedding a dead service hostname, with the proportion that have a known replacement
entries.custody: scattered community servers

entries.name: Nintendo Wi-Fi Connection (closed 2014-05-20)
entries.what_dies: the service; DS and Wii titles that used it lost online play and, for some, the only way to obtain content

evidence.source: prior knowledge; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: a community replacement service keeps a subset alive on modded hardware
entries.guardian: Record which titles needed the service for single-player content, because those are not 'multiplayer losses' at all
entries.gate: a per-title table: online-only content, still reachable yes/no, and the mechanism
entries.custody: one volunteer project -- a single point of failure the register names

entries.name: Google Stadia (2019-2023)
entries.what_dies: the service, and with it the only copy of anything that was Stadia-exclusive; the player never held a file

evidence.source: Phil Harrison, 'A message about Stadia and our long term streaming strategy'

entries.survivors: most titles were ports; the exclusives are the question and the announcement says nothing about them
entries.guardian: Keep the register's list of Stadia-only titles with what happened to each, and mark unknown rather than assuming they were ported
entries.gate: a list where every entry has a status (ported / lost / unknown) and a citation, with the unknown count printed
entries.custody: nobody known for the exclusives

entries.name: Games for Windows Live marketplace (closed 2013)
entries.what_dies: the storefront and the licence service; purchases became unverifiable and some titles refused to launch without the client

evidence.source: prior knowledge; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: patches that strip the client exist for the popular titles
entries.guardian: Record which titles cannot start without the dead client, because a patch existing is not the same as a patch being applied
entries.gate: a count of affected titles with a verified working patch, run once per title
entries.custody: the patching community

entries.name: Flappy Bird (2014)
entries.what_dies: the author pulled it from the stores at the height of its popularity; installs that already existed kept working, and everyone else lost access in a day
entries.event: 2014-02-09: removed from the iOS and Android stores by its author

evidence.source: prior knowledge of the removal; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: clones (many), and pre-existing installs on old devices; the original binary circulates unofficially
entries.guardian: Record the class, not the title: the lesson is that a store listing is not a deposit, so the register asks every mobile entry who holds the binary
entries.gate: one archived build with a hash and a named custodian, or an explicit 'nobody known'
entries.custody: unofficial APK mirrors; the register treats them as unverified

entries.name: Infinity Blade (2010-2018)
entries.what_dies: delisted from the App Store; an iOS game that cannot be reinstalled on a current device, so the only copies are on hardware that can no longer be updated

evidence.source: prior knowledge of the delisting; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: installs on unsupported hardware; IPA archives of uncertain provenance
entries.guardian: Image one known-good install per device generation before the hardware dies, because that is the only copy that will ever exist
entries.gate: an image per generation with a hash and the device model recorded, plus a launch check
entries.custody: collectors holding old devices; no archive has a mandate

entries.name: The 32-bit iOS purge (2017)
entries.what_dies: iOS 11 refused to run 32-bit apps at all; tens of thousands of games stopped launching on any device that could still be updated, with no per-title decision and no notice period

evidence.source: prior knowledge of the OS change; the affected-title count is not measured here

entries.survivors: old devices held below iOS 11; IPA archives for a fraction of the catalogue
entries.guardian: Count the affected titles from a store catalogue snapshot, so the class has a size rather than a reputation
entries.gate: a count of 32-bit-only titles from a dated catalogue snapshot, with the surviving-build proportion
entries.custody: nobody known at catalogue scale; this is the register's largest single unknown

entries.name: Flash games (ended 2020-12-31)
entries.what_dies: the plugin. Adobe ended support on 2020-12-31 and browsers removed the capability, so a catalogue of tens of thousands of games stopped existing in the same week

evidence.source: Adobe Flash Player End of Life

entries.survivors: Flashpoint and similar archives keep a playable subset; the long tail was never captured
entries.guardian: Count what the archives actually hold against the catalogues that still list titles, so the gap is a number
entries.gate: a gap count: titles listed by a dead portal minus titles playable in an archive
entries.custody: two large volunteer archives

entries.name: Shockwave / Macromedia Director titles
entries.what_dies: the player and the authoring tool both: Director is discontinued, so not only can the files not run, they cannot be re-exported
entries.event: ongoing: the runtime is discontinued and the plugin is gone from browsers

evidence.source: prior knowledge; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: emulation of the Director runtime exists and is partial
entries.guardian: Record the runtime version each archived title needs, because a Director file without its version is a guess
entries.gate: a manifest where every title names its runtime version and the archive that holds it
entries.custody: one project; thin

entries.name: Java applet games
entries.what_dies: browsers removed the plugin interface; an applet needs a JRE, a browser that still speaks NPAPI, and a signed jar that has not expired

evidence.source: prior knowledge; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: applet archives and a standalone runner; most portals' catalogues are gone
entries.guardian: Extract the applet payload from dead portals' archives before the portals' CDNs expire
entries.gate: a harvest count of applet jars retrieved, with a runnable proportion measured
entries.custody: scattered; no mandate

entries.name: Unity Web Player games (2000s-2010s)
entries.what_dies: the plugin was discontinued in favour of WebGL builds; a .unity3d file needs the plugin, and many web games were never rebuilt

evidence.source: prior knowledge; the retirement date is not re-verified here

entries.survivors: some builds were re-exported to WebGL; the rest are files nobody can run
entries.guardian: Name which archived builds are WebGL-capable and which are plugin-only, because only one of those two lists is playable
entries.gate: a two-list split with counts and the runtime version per file
entries.custody: portal archives; decaying

entries.name: Satellaview broadcast content (1995-2000)
entries.what_dies: the broadcasts. Episodes were transmitted on a schedule and never sold; when the service ended there was no cartridge to keep

evidence.source: prior knowledge; the completeness of surviving recordings is unmeasured

entries.survivors: partial recordings held by hobbyists; some sound-link audio survives only as off-air tape
entries.guardian: Record which titles are known only from screenshots and press coverage, and mark them lost rather than 'rare'
entries.gate: a title-by-title existence table with a citation or an explicit 'no artefact known'
entries.custody: a handful of hobbyists; the register cannot name them

entries.name: Sega Channel (1994-1998)
entries.what_dies: the cable delivery; games arrived over a TV channel into a cartridge that held them only while powered, so nothing was ever owned

evidence.source: prior knowledge; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: the underlying Genesis games mostly survive elsewhere; the service itself does not
entries.guardian: Record that the games survive and the service does not, so the register does not overstate the loss
entries.gate: a mapping of the service's catalogue to surviving cartridge equivalents, with the unmatched count
entries.custody: nobody; the service is gone

entries.name: Nintendo Power rewritable cartridges (1988-1991)
entries.what_dies: the cartridges were rewritable and were meant to be overwritten; each new download destroyed the last, and the service wrote over its own history

evidence.source: prior knowledge; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: a very small number of carts that were never overwritten; several titles are known from no complete dump
entries.guardian: Treat every surviving cart as a unique artefact and image it before it is used, because using it destroys the thing being preserved
entries.gate: an image-first procedure per cart, with a hash recorded before and after any use
entries.custody: a few collectors in Japan

entries.name: SafeDisc / SecuROM disc checks (Windows)
entries.what_dies: the OS. Windows 10 dropped the driver these disc checks needed, so legally bought discs stopped launching on a current machine

evidence.source: prior knowledge of the update; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: patched executables exist for popular titles; the check itself cannot be reproduced
entries.guardian: Record the affected titles as a class rather than title by title, and count how many have a working patch
entries.gate: a class count plus a patched proportion, measured by launching each title once
entries.custody: the patching community; no institution holds a licence to fix these

entries.name: StarForce-protected titles
entries.what_dies: a driver that modern Windows refuses to load, and a disc check bound to physical media geometry

evidence.source: prior knowledge; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: patches for some titles; others have no route at all
entries.guardian: Name the titles with no patch, because those are the ones a player cannot lawfully run on any current machine
entries.gate: a list of unpatched titles, each with a tested launch attempt on a current OS
entries.custody: scattered; no mandate

entries.name: Always-online activation for single-player games
entries.what_dies: the activation server; a single-player game becomes unplayable when a company decides the title is old
entries.event: ongoing: no commitment from any vendor to publish an offline path

evidence.source: prior knowledge of the practice; no dated vendor statement cited

entries.survivors: the game files, which are useless without the check
entries.guardian: Ask for the one thing that costs a vendor nothing and saves the title: a documented offline unlock at end of support
entries.gate: a count of vendors who have published such a path, and the titles it covers
entries.custody: the vendors, by contract; this is the register's clearest live dependency

entries.name: Code wheels, codewords and lens devices
entries.what_dies: the artefact itself. A lens device or a printed wheel that was thrown away with the box makes a working disk unplayable forever
entries.event: ongoing: the artefact and the software are separated by time

evidence.source: prior knowledge; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: scans of some wheels and manuals exist; many are undocumented
entries.guardian: Image every protection artefact the register meets, at 600 dpi, because a scan is the only form in which it can travel
entries.gate: count of protection artefacts imaged, with the resolution and the title each belongs to
entries.custody: collectors; unsystematic

entries.name: Manual-lookup copy protection
entries.what_dies: the manual. 'Type the fourth word on page 12' means the software is worthless without the booklet, and booklets were discarded
entries.event: ongoing: the manuals are the scarce artefact, not the disks

evidence.source: prior knowledge; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: manual scans at replacementdocs-class archives; coverage is partial
entries.guardian: Cross-reference the register's entries against manual archives and count the games whose manual has no scan
entries.gate: a coverage percentage computed from the entry list, not estimated
entries.custody: volunteer scan archives

entries.name: Undocumented PAL/GAL logic on arcade boards
entries.what_dies: the programmable logic whose fuse map was never published; when a board's chip dies, the board cannot be rebuilt even with every other part
entries.event: ongoing: boards fail and the logic was never read out

evidence.source: prior knowledge of the practice; the undumped count is unmeasured here

entries.survivors: dumps exist for some boards, held by individuals; no complete census
entries.guardian: Advocate read-out-before-repair: image the logic before desoldering, because a repaired board with a new PAL is a different board
entries.gate: count of boards where the logic was imaged before repair, out of boards repaired
entries.custody: a few specialists

entries.name: Console BIOS and firmware dumps
entries.what_dies: a console that needs a firmware dump to boot, where the dump cannot lawfully be distributed, so every user must extract it from their own machine
entries.event: ongoing: dumps survive, distribution is restricted

evidence.source: prior knowledge; the legal position varies by jurisdiction and is not re-verified here

entries.survivors: dumps are archived; the machines that can produce them are the constraint
entries.guardian: Ship the extraction procedure per console so a player can make their own dump, since shipping the dump is not available
entries.gate: one extraction procedure per console that this estate has actually run, with the hash of the result
entries.custody: archives hold the dumps; users hold the machines

entries.name: XNA / Xbox Live Indie Games (2007-2017)
entries.what_dies: the toolchain and the store together: XNA was discontinued, the indie channel closed, and the games were never distributed as files

evidence.source: prior knowledge; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: some titles were ported to other engines by their authors; the rest have no distribution channel
entries.guardian: Record the authors' own builds where they exist, because the store is gone and the authors are the only custodians
entries.gate: a per-title custody field: author build located / port located / nobody known
entries.custody: the authors, individually

entries.name: RenderWare-era middleware
entries.what_dies: middleware licences that cannot be renewed, and authoring tools whose installers no longer run, so surviving source cannot be rebuilt

evidence.source: prior knowledge; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: shipped binaries; rebuilding is the part that is dying
entries.guardian: Record for each shard-eligible title whether a rebuild is possible from what survives, because a binary is not a source
entries.gate: a rebuild-possible flag per title, set only after an attempted build
entries.custody: unclear; the register marks this class as its weakest

entries.name: Console SDK signing and dev hardware
entries.what_dies: signing keys and development kits that were never sold; without them, code cannot run on the original hardware even when everything else survives
entries.event: ongoing: SDKs are under NDA and hardware is decommissioned

evidence.source: prior knowledge; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: exploits that allow unsigned code on many systems; not on all
entries.guardian: Name which systems still cannot run unsigned code, because those are the ones where the shard contract needs an emulated host rather than hardware
entries.gate: a per-system table: unsigned code possible yes/no, and the mechanism or the refusal
entries.custody: the scene, per system

entries.name: ZSNES (last release 2007)
entries.what_dies: the emulator, abandoned while still the fastest option on old hardware; its accuracy limits are undocumented outside its own source

evidence.source: prior knowledge of the project; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: source code in the open, so the tool can be revived; most users moved to other emulators
entries.guardian: Record which titles only this emulator still runs at usable speed on low-end hardware, because that is the capability the replacement has to match
entries.gate: a speed comparison per title on the reference low-end box, old tool vs replacement
entries.custody: public source; unmaintained

entries.name: Bleem! (1999-2001)
entries.what_dies: a commercial emulator litigated out of the market; the precedent survived, the product did not

evidence.source: prior knowledge; the case citation is not re-verified here

entries.survivors: retail copies, no source, no support
entries.guardian: Keep the case record in the register, because the precedent is what makes every other route lawful and it is cited more often than it is read
entries.gate: a citation with its holding summarised in one line and a source tier
entries.custody: collectors; the legal record is public

entries.name: Laserdisc arcade games (1983)
entries.what_dies: the player and the disc together: laserdisc rot is real, the players are unrepairable, and the game logic waited on a video source that no longer spins

evidence.source: prior knowledge; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: video captures made from working players; Daphne-class reimplementations exist
entries.guardian: Require a capture whose source disc is named, because a capture of a rotted disc is a capture of the rot
entries.gate: a per-title record: disc identity, capture hash, player model used
entries.custody: a small number of collectors and one reconstruction project

entries.name: Soldered SRAM save batteries
entries.what_dies: a coin cell that has been draining since manufacture; the save dies first and the leak damages the board after
entries.event: ongoing: every cart is past its design life

evidence.source: prior knowledge; the failure census is unmeasured here

entries.survivors: the games; the saves are the perishable content and most were never imaged
entries.guardian: Ship a save extractor before the battery dies, and treat an unextracted save as a loss in progress rather than a backup waiting to happen
entries.gate: saves extracted per title, and the number of titles where none exists
entries.custody: whoever holds the cart

entries.name: Early CD and DVD pressings
entries.what_dies: binder and reflective-layer failure in early pressings; the data is intact until it is not, and the failure is visible only as unreadable sectors
entries.event: ongoing: pressings from the 1980s-1990s are past their expected life

evidence.source: prior knowledge; no measured rot rate on this box

entries.survivors: images made before the rot; the discs behind them are the clock
entries.guardian: Image on first contact and keep two copies on different media, because a single image is a single point of failure wearing a backup's clothes
entries.gate: an error-rate reading per disc (C2/C1 counts or equivalent) recorded with the image's hash
entries.custody: archives; unevenly

entries.name: Flash-cartridge charge decay
entries.what_dies: the charge in a NAND cell; a cart left unpowered for years loses its save, and in the worst documented cases its own code
entries.event: ongoing: retention is a specification, not a promise

evidence.source: prior knowledge; the retention figures are datasheet claims, not measurements here

entries.survivors: dumps and save images; the physical carts are the constraint
entries.guardian: Record a power-on-and-image schedule for the register's flash-based systems, because retention is refreshed by use and by copying
entries.gate: a schedule with the last image date per cart family, and the count past due
entries.custody: collectors; nobody holds a mandate for a refresh cycle

entries.name: EPROM bit rot in arcade and cartridge hardware
entries.what_dies: the floating gate, slowly; a 40-year-old EPROM can lose a bit and the board boots wrong in a way nobody can diagnose
entries.event: ongoing: every original EPROM is ageing

evidence.source: prior knowledge; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: dumps verified against a second source; the 'good' set is the thing that must be verified, not assumed
entries.guardian: Verify every dump against two independent sources and record which dumps have only one witness
entries.gate: a single-witness dump count computed from the manifest
entries.custody: the dumping scene; the register names single-witness dumps as its top re-dump priority

entries.name: CRT-dependent display hardware
entries.what_dies: the displays: light guns that need a raster, 15 kHz sync that modern panels refuse, and CRTs that are no longer manufactured and cannot be shipped
entries.event: ongoing: no CRT production; the installed base is shrinking

evidence.source: prior knowledge; the installed-base size is unmeasured

entries.survivors: up-scalers and FPGA line-doublers; a shrinking but real repair scene
entries.guardian: Record the display timing a title depends on as part of its recipe, so 'it looks wrong' becomes a measurable statement about sync
entries.gate: a per-title timing record (lines, refresh, sync) and a capture compared against it
entries.custody: collectors and one or two manufacturers of up-scalers

entries.name: Vectrex (1982) and vector displays
entries.what_dies: the vector CRT and its deflection circuitry; a vector monitor cannot be replaced by a raster panel without changing what the game looks like
entries.event: ongoing: displays fail and are not repairable at scale

evidence.source: prior knowledge; not fetched this session

entries.survivors: dumps and a small homebrew scene; a handful of working machines
entries.guardian: Express a vector game as a display list of line segments, which is exactly what an integer sim can emit and any host can draw
entries.gate: a title re-presented from an emitted segment list, with a frame hash compared against a capture of the original
entries.custody: a small collector base
